name: ASSET_RESERVE_ATTESTATION
description: Verifies cryptographic proof-of-reserves and custodial bank confirmations backing stablecoins and tokenized assets.

intents.name: ASSET_RESERVE_ATTESTATION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a stablecoin, tokenized asset or custodian and asks whether attested reserves back the circulating supply, cross-checking on-chain balances against a custodian or proof-of-reserves feed. Example: "Do the attested reserves behind USDC cover its circulating supply as of the latest proof-of-reserves report?" → ASSET_RESERVE_ATTESTATION_GENERAL. Not: "What is USDC trading at?" (a price) → CRYPTO_PRICE_USD. Not: "How much USDC does this address hold?" (one address's balance) → WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK_GENERAL.

name: B2B_IDENTITY_ENRICHMENT
description: Enriches business entity records with corporate tax IDs, headquarters addresses, executive listings, and domain validation.

intents.name: B2B_IDENTITY_ENRICHMENT_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies a partial business record - a domain, brand or work email - and asks for it to be filled out with firmographic fields: legal entity, tax id, headquarters, headcount, industry, executives, domain validity. Example: "Enrich acme.io: legal entity name, tax ID, HQ address, employee count and CEO." → B2B_IDENTITY_ENRICHMENT_GENERAL. Not: "Is Acme Ltd incorporated, and who is its registered agent?" (the official register record itself) → CORPORATE_REGISTRY_LOOKUP_GENERAL.

name: CARRIER_SERVICEABILITY
description: Evaluates freight and courier delivery coverage, weight limits, and hazardous material restrictions for target routes.

intents.name: CARRIER_SERVICEABILITY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks whether a carrier will carry a given shipment on a given lane at all: coverage, weight and dimension limits, hazardous material restrictions. Example: "Will any carrier take a 68 kg lithium-battery shipment from 94107 to rural 59718, and under what restrictions?" → CARRIER_SERVICEABILITY_GENERAL. Not: "What would that shipment cost and when would it land?" (rates and ETA on a lane already known serviceable) → SHIP_RATE_ETA_GENERAL.

name: CODE_PATCH_VERIFY
description: Validates that software patch commits compile, resolve targeted defects, and introduce no regression side effects.

intents.name: CODE_PATCH_VERIFY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies a patch, commit or branch and asks for a mechanical verdict: does it build, does the suite pass, is the named defect fixed, does anything regress. Example: "Apply this patch, run the build and test suite in a sandbox, and report whether it exits zero with the defect fixed and no regressions." → CODE_PATCH_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "Is this patch a sound approach?" (a judgment about the change) → CODE_REVIEW_GENERAL. Not: "Run the full suite against build 4412 and tell me what broke since the last green run." (regression sweep of an existing build, not verification of one patch) → REGRESSION_VERIFY_GENERAL.

name: CODE_REVIEW
description: Evaluates source code pull requests against internal architectural patterns, maintainability standards, and syntax rules.

intents.name: CODE_REVIEW_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies source code, a diff or a pull request and asks for a review of design, maintainability, readability or architectural fit. The output is an opinion, not a build result. Example: "Review this pull request for maintainability and whether it fits our service architecture: <diff>." → CODE_REVIEW_GENERAL. Not: "Does this patch compile and pass the test suite?" (a mechanical build/test verdict) → CODE_PATCH_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "Does this code leak secrets or pull vulnerable dependencies?" (a security scan) → SECURITY_REVIEW_GENERAL.

name: COMMERCE_PURCHASE_VERIFY
description: Verifies the authenticity, item line totals, and payment authorization for a completed e-commerce purchase transaction.

intents.name: COMMERCE_PURCHASE_VERIFY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies an order id, receipt or payment reference and asks whether that purchase genuinely exists and matches stated line items, totals and payment authorization. Example: "Verify order 114-3941-8820: does the merchant show these three line items, a $148.20 total and an authorized payment?" → COMMERCE_PURCHASE_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "Is the card ending 4242 valid and active?" (an instrument check with no order) → PAYMENT_METHOD_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "Can I still return this order?" (policy eligibility) → RETURN_POLICY_VERIFY_GENERAL.

name: CONTRACT_OBLIGATION_AUDIT
description: Parses and verifies legal contract milestone deliverables, payment terms, and vendor performance commitments.

intents.name: CONTRACT_OBLIGATION_AUDIT_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies contract text and asks what obligations it creates - deliverables, milestones, payment terms, performance commitments - or whether those have been met. Example: "Extract every deliverable, due date and payment milestone from this MSA and flag the ones already overdue." → CONTRACT_OBLIGATION_AUDIT_GENERAL. Not: "Is this signed PDF genuine and unaltered?" (integrity of the artifact, not the terms inside it) → DOCUMENT_AUTHENTICITY_GENERAL. Not: "Does this invoice tie out against the PO?" (ledger reconciliation) → INVOICE_LEDGER_RECONCILE_GENERAL.

name: CORPORATE_REGISTRY_LOOKUP
description: Queries national business registers for incorporation status, registered agent details, and beneficial ownership filings.

intents.name: CORPORATE_REGISTRY_LOOKUP_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a company and asks for its official register record: incorporation status, company number, registered address or agent, directors, beneficial owners. Example: "What is the incorporation status and registered agent for UK company number 12345678?" → CORPORATE_REGISTRY_LOOKUP_GENERAL. Not: "Fill out this company record with its tax ID, headcount and executive contacts." (commercial enrichment beyond the register) → B2B_IDENTITY_ENRICHMENT_GENERAL.

name: CROSS_CHAIN_STATE_VERIFY
description: Proves cryptographic Merkle-Patricia state roots and cross-chain message execution headers between distinct blockchain networks.

intents.name: CROSS_CHAIN_STATE_VERIFY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks whether a state root, Merkle-Patricia proof, block header or bridge message from one chain verifies against another. Requires two named chains and a specific proof, header or message. Example: "Verify that the LayerZero message with nonce 4412 from arbitrum executed on base and that the committed state root matches." → CROSS_CHAIN_STATE_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "How do cross-chain bridges work?" (conceptual, nothing supplied to verify) → CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL.
intents.onchain_note: the intent has no response format

name: CUSTOMER_TICKET_RESOLUTION
description: Analyzes helpdesk support interactions, resolution accuracy, agent action compliance, and customer satisfaction outcomes.

intents.name: CUSTOMER_TICKET_RESOLUTION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies a support conversation or ticket and asks how well it was handled: whether the issue was actually resolved, whether policy was followed, likely customer satisfaction. Example: "Here is a support thread: was the customer's issue resolved, and did the agent follow refund policy?" → CUSTOMER_TICKET_RESOLUTION_GENERAL. Not: "Was the first response inside the 4-hour SLA?" (a timing threshold) → SLA_COMPLIANCE_GENERAL.

name: DATACENTER_TELEMETRY_VERIFY
description: Audits rack power usage effectiveness (PUE), server thermal telemetry, and backup generator readiness metrics.

intents.name: DATACENTER_TELEMETRY_VERIFY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks for facility or rack telemetry at a named site: power usage effectiveness, power draw, inlet and thermal readings, cooling or backup generator readiness. Example: "What is the current PUE and rack inlet temperature in hall 2, and is the backup generator in ready state?" → DATACENTER_TELEMETRY_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "Is device 44's sensor payload signed correctly and in calibration?" (edge device telemetry integrity) → SENSOR_TELEMETRY_VERIFY_GENERAL.

name: DELIVERY_WINDOW_VERIFY
description: Confirms driver dispatch route scheduling, customer delivery appointment slots, and signature requirements.

intents.name: DELIVERY_WINDOW_VERIFY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks what delivery appointment window, route slot or signature requirement a dispatch system has committed for a stop or order. Example: "What appointment window is scheduled for order 8841 on tomorrow's route, and does it require a signature?" → DELIVERY_WINDOW_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "Where is the parcel right now?" (carrier scan events) → PACKAGE_STATUS_GENERAL.

name: DOCUMENT_AUTHENTICITY
description: Validates digital certificate signatures, notarizations, tamper-evident seals, and document checksum integrity.

intents.name: DOCUMENT_AUTHENTICITY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies a document plus its signature, seal or timestamp data and asks whether it is genuine and unaltered: certificate chain, notarization, tamper-evident seal, checksum. Example: "Verify the digital signature and notarization seal on this PDF and tell me whether the content changed after signing." → DOCUMENT_AUTHENTICITY_GENERAL. Not: "Is this image AI-generated or spliced?" (media forensics) → MEDIA_FORENSIC_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "What obligations does this contract create?" (reading the contents) → CONTRACT_OBLIGATION_AUDIT_GENERAL.

name: EMAIL_SECURITY
description: Verifies SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records, inspects header anomalies, and detects spoofing or malicious attachments.

intents.name: EMAIL_SECURITY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies a domain or an email message and asks about mail authentication and spoofing: SPF, DKIM and DMARC records, header anomalies, malicious attachments. Example: "Does example.com publish valid SPF, DKIM and DMARC records, and do these message headers indicate spoofing?" → EMAIL_SECURITY_GENERAL. Not: "Is the link inside that email on a blocklist?" (URL reputation) → URL_SAFE_GENERAL. Not: "Is the attached binary malicious?" (a file verdict) → MALWARE_DETECTION_HASH.

name: EVENT_OUTCOME_RESOLUTION
description: Resolves objective real-world event outcomes for prediction markets and conditional contracts using quorum oracles.

intents.name: EVENT_OUTCOME_RESOLUTION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a specific real-world event with a settled or settleable outcome (an election, a fixture, a flight, a contract condition) and asks what the outcome actually was, for a prediction market or conditional contract to resolve against. Requires a named, checkable event. Example: "Did flight UA328 on 2026-03-11 land before 18:00 local? Resolve this market." → EVENT_OUTCOME_RESOLUTION_GENERAL. Not: "Who do you think will win the election?" (asks for a prediction, not the resolution of a determinable event) → CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL. Not: "Who won the Lakers vs Celtics game last night?" (a plain sports result with no market to settle) → GAME_RESULT_GENERAL.

name: FARE_RULE_VERIFY
description: Inspects fare terms, baggage allowances, cancellation penalties, and change fee stipulations for booked travel tickets.

intents.name: FARE_RULE_VERIFY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a ticket, fare or booking and asks what its rules permit: baggage allowance, change fees, cancellation penalties, refundability. Example: "For this booked fare, what checked baggage is included and what is the change fee to move the date?" → FARE_RULE_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "What seats are available on that route?" (inventory) → FLIGHT_AVAILABILITY_GENERAL. Not: "Can I return this purchase?" (a retail return policy) → RETURN_POLICY_VERIFY_GENERAL.

name: FLIGHT_AVAILABILITY
description: Queries real-time airline schedule networks, cabin seat inventories, and booking fare class statuses.

intents.name: FLIGHT_AVAILABILITY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a route or flight and dates and asks what seats, cabins or fare classes are bookable. Example: "What economy seats are available on SFO-JFK next Tuesday morning, and in which fare classes?" → FLIGHT_AVAILABILITY_GENERAL. Not: "Is my flight delayed today?" (operational disruption) → TRAVEL_DISRUPTION_GENERAL. Not: "What baggage allowance does that fare include?" (fare terms) → FARE_RULE_VERIFY_GENERAL.

name: FRAUD_RISK
description: Computes real-time behavioral fraud probability scores using device fingerprinting, IP geolocation, and transaction context.

intents.name: FRAUD_RISK_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies actor context - device fingerprint, IP, email, signup or session behaviour - and asks for a forward-looking probability that the actor is fraudulent. There is no ground truth at query time; the answer is a score. Example: "Score the fraud risk of this signup: IP 45.83.x.x, headless browser fingerprint, disposable email domain." → FRAUD_RISK_GENERAL. Not: "Is this specific transaction from 0xabc... fraudulent?" (an assessment of one concrete thing that already happened) → FRAUD_DETECTION_GENERAL. Not: "Where is IP 45.83.x.x located?" (a plain geolocation lookup) → IP_GEOLOCATION_GENERAL.

name: FX_NOW
description: Provides real-time institutional foreign exchange mid-market rates, spreads, and currency conversion quotes.

intents.name: FX_NOW_CAD
intents.description: Query asks for the live institutional mid-market rate between the US dollar and the Canadian dollar (USD/CAD or CAD/USD), as a market data point with no amount to convert. Example: "What is the current USD/CAD mid-market rate?" → FX_NOW_CAD. Not: a pair without both USD and CAD (another FX_NOW_ intent). Not: "How much is 100 USD in CAD?" (a conversion of a stated amount for a user).

intents.name: FX_NOW_EUR
intents.description: Query asks for the live institutional mid-market rate between the US dollar and the euro (USD/EUR or EUR/USD), as a market data point with no amount to convert. Example: "What is the current EUR/USD mid-market rate?" → FX_NOW_EUR. Not: a pair without both USD and EUR (another FX_NOW_ intent). Not: "How much is 100 USD in EUR?" (a conversion of a stated amount for a user).

intents.name: FX_NOW_SEK
intents.description: Query asks for the live institutional mid-market rate between the US dollar and the Swedish krona (USD/SEK or SEK/USD), as a market data point with no amount to convert. Example: "What is the current USD/SEK mid-market rate?" → FX_NOW_SEK. Not: a pair without both USD and SEK (another FX_NOW_ intent). Not: "How much is 100 USD in SEK?" (a conversion of a stated amount for a user).

name: GRID_POWER_PRICE
description: Ingests real-time nodal marginal locational prices (LMP) and day-ahead electricity spot rates from regional grid operators.

intents.name: GRID_POWER_PRICE_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a grid, node, hub or region and asks for electricity prices from the operator: locational marginal price, day-ahead or real-time spot rates. Example: "What is the current locational marginal price at the ERCOT Houston hub, and what did day-ahead settle at?" → GRID_POWER_PRICE_GENERAL. Not: "What is a token or commodity trading at?" (market instrument prices) → CRYPTO_PRICE_USD or FINANCIAL_DATA_GENERAL.

name: HOTEL_AVAILABILITY
description: Confirms room inventory, nightly rates, amenities, and cancellation policies across hospitality property management systems.

intents.name: HOTEL_AVAILABILITY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a property, city and dates and asks what rooms are available, at what nightly rate and under what cancellation terms. Example: "What king rooms are open at this Austin property for March 3-5, at what nightly rate, and are they refundable?" → HOTEL_AVAILABILITY_GENERAL. Not: "Is my reservation still being held?" (an existing booking lock) → TRAVEL_TRANSIT_LOCK_GENERAL.

name: INVOICE_LEDGER_RECONCILE
description: Performs automated 3-way matching between invoice line items, purchase orders, and receiving dock receipts.

intents.name: INVOICE_LEDGER_RECONCILE_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies invoices, purchase orders and receipts and asks whether they reconcile: three-way match on line items, quantities, tax and totals, and which entries do not tie out. Example: "Three-way match invoice INV-8841 against PO-2231 and the goods receipt, and list the mismatched lines." → INVOICE_LEDGER_RECONCILE_GENERAL. Not: "Does PO-2231 exist with the approved amount and budget?" (the purchase order on its own) → PURCHASE_ORDER_VERIFY_GENERAL.

name: KYC_BIOMETRIC_LIVENESS
description: Verifies user selfie liveness video capture against government photo IDs to prevent spoofing fraud.

intents.name: KYC_BIOMETRIC_LIVENESS_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies a selfie, liveness capture or video plus an identity document and asks whether the subject is a live human matching that document rather than a mask, print or replay. Requires actual media. Example: "Here is a selfie video and a passport scan: is this a live capture of the document holder, or a spoof?" → KYC_BIOMETRIC_LIVENESS_GENERAL. Not: "Is this photo AI-generated?" (media authenticity with no identity document to match against) → MEDIA_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK_GENERAL.

name: LIQUIDITY_DEPTH_VERIFY
description: Measures bid-ask order book depth, cumulative slippage bands, and market maker liquidity across decentralized pools.

intents.name: LIQUIDITY_DEPTH_VERIFY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a market, pair or pool and asks for order book depth, bid-ask spread, or the slippage a stated trade size would incur at a point in time. Example: "What is the bid-ask depth and expected slippage on a 50 ETH sell into the WETH/USDC pool on base right now?" → LIQUIDITY_DEPTH_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "How much total value is locked in that pool?" (a TVL total, not depth at a size) → TVL_LOOKUP_GENERAL. Not: "Which venue should I route this trade through?" (a routing decision) → OPTIMAL_EXECUTION_ROUTE_GENERAL.

name: LIVE_PORT_CONGESTION
description: Measures commercial container port vessel queue wait times, berth occupancy ratios, and dwell day averages.

intents.name: LIVE_PORT_CONGESTION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a seaport or terminal and asks how congested it is: vessels waiting at anchor, berth occupancy, average dwell time. Example: "How many container vessels are at anchor off Long Beach, and what is average berth dwell time this week?" → LIVE_PORT_CONGESTION_GENERAL. Not: "Where is vessel IMO 9321483 right now?" (one ship's position) → VESSEL_TELEMETRY_VERIFY_GENERAL.

name: LIVE_SHELF_PRICE
description: Fetches and verifies current live shelf or retail listing prices across online merchant catalogs and marketplaces.

intents.name: LIVE_SHELF_PRICE_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a retail product, SKU or listing and asks what it currently sells for at one or more merchants. Example: "What is the current listed price of the Sony WH-1000XM5 at Amazon and Walmart right now?" → LIVE_SHELF_PRICE_GENERAL. Not: "What is Sony's share price?" (an equity quote) → STOCK_PRICE_US_EQUITY. Not: "Is that model actually in stock?" (availability, not price) → SKU_IN_STOCK_GENERAL.

name: LLM_OUTPUT_EVALUATION
description: Evaluates generative model responses against factual ground truth, citation fidelity, hallucination markers, and safety guardrails.

intents.name: LLM_OUTPUT_EVALUATION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies a generative model's output and asks for it to be judged: factual fidelity, citation support, hallucination markers, tone or safety, usually against the prompt or a reference. Example: "Here is a model answer and its cited sources: rate it for factual accuracy, citation support and hallucination." → LLM_OUTPUT_EVALUATION_GENERAL. Not: "Was this paragraph written by an AI or a human?" (authorship detection, not quality) → AI_TEXT_DETECTION_GENERAL. Not: "Did the agent complete this task correctly?" (scoring an execution against a rubric) → TASK_EXECUTION_QUALITY_GENERAL.

name: MACRO_ECONOMIC_INDICATOR
description: Aggregates released central bank interest rates, consumer price index (CPI) updates, and unemployment figures.

intents.name: MACRO_ECONOMIC_INDICATOR_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a published macroeconomic statistic for a country or region - policy rate, CPI, unemployment, GDP - and asks for its released value or latest print. Example: "What was the latest US CPI year-over-year print, and what is the current federal funds target range?" → MACRO_ECONOMIC_INDICATOR_GENERAL. Not: "What is EUR/USD right now?" (a live market rate) → one of FX_NOW_EUR, FX_NOW_CAD, FX_NOW_SEK. Not: "What is Apple's revenue growth this quarter?" (company fundamentals) → FINANCIAL_DATA_GENERAL.

name: MALWARE_DETECTION
description: Scans file hashes and binaries against multi-engine antivirus definitions and sandbox behavioral detonation traces.

intents.name: MALWARE_DETECTION_HASH
intents.description: Query supplies a file hash (SHA-256, SHA-1 or MD5) and asks whether the file is malicious according to antivirus engines or known-malware databases. Example: "Is SHA-256 275a021bbfb6489e54d471899f7db9d1663fc695ec2fe2a2c4538aabf651fd0f flagged as malware?" → MALWARE_DETECTION_HASH. Not: "Is this URL on a phishing blocklist?" → URL_SCAN_VERDICT.

name: MEDIA_FORENSIC_VERIFY
description: Detects AI deepfake artifacts, EXIF metadata manipulation, and generative audio/video synthesis in media uploads.

intents.name: MEDIA_FORENSIC_VERIFY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies an image, audio or video file and asks for forensic analysis of manipulation: generative artifacts, splices, EXIF and metadata inconsistency, synthetic speech. Requires actual media. Example: "Run forensics on this audio clip: is the voice synthetic, and does the file metadata match the claimed capture date?" → MEDIA_FORENSIC_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "Is the face in this video a deepfake?" (face swap specifically) → DEEPFAKE_DETECTION_GENERAL. Not: "Is this photo real or AI-generated?" (the broad authenticity question) → MEDIA_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK_GENERAL.

name: MINING_HASHPRICE_VERIFY
description: Calculates instantaneous proof-of-work mining revenue per unit of hashing power based on block rewards and network difficulty.

intents.name: MINING_HASHPRICE_VERIFY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks what a unit of hashing power currently earns on a proof-of-work network, derived from block reward, fees and network difficulty. Example: "What is Bitcoin hashprice per PH/s per day at current difficulty and fee levels?" → MINING_HASHPRICE_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "What is Bitcoin trading at?" (an asset quote) → CRYPTO_PRICE_USD. Not: "What is power costing at that hub?" (electricity prices) → GRID_POWER_PRICE_GENERAL.

name: ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY
description: Validates smart contract event logs, gas consumption, token balances, and wallet transaction states directly on-chain.

intents.name: ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks for a specific value read from a blockchain node at a stated block height or 'latest': an event log field, gas consumed, a contract view or storage value, a contract-held token balance. The block or 'latest' anchor is what distinguishes it. Example: "At block 21000000 on ethereum, what amount did the Transfer log in tx 0xabc... carry, and how much gas did that tx use?" → ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "What was the status of transaction 0xabc...?" (a transaction lookup, not a named metric at a height) → ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP_GENERAL. Not: "What is the balance of vitalik.eth?" (a plain wallet balance) → WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK_GENERAL.

name: OPTIMAL_EXECUTION_ROUTE
description: Determines optimal multi-venue order execution routing to minimize slippage, exchange fees, and market impact.

intents.name: OPTIMAL_EXECUTION_ROUTE_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks for the best venue or multi-hop path to execute a stated trade size, judged on slippage, fees and market impact. Requires both an asset pair and a size. Example: "What is the best route to swap 250,000 USDC into WETH on base right now, minimising slippage and fees?" → OPTIMAL_EXECUTION_ROUTE_GENERAL. Not: "What is WETH trading at?" (a quote, no execution decision) → CRYPTO_PRICE_USD. Not: "How deep is that pool at a 50 ETH size?" (measuring depth, not choosing a route) → LIQUIDITY_DEPTH_VERIFY_GENERAL.

name: PACKAGE_STATUS
description: Tracks real-time parcel checkpoint milestones, courier custody transfers, and delivery progress across logistics carriers.

intents.name: PACKAGE_STATUS_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies a tracking number or shipment reference and asks where the parcel is and what its latest carrier scan events are. Example: "Where is tracking number 1Z999AA10123456784 now, and what was the last scan event?" → PACKAGE_STATUS_GENERAL. Not: "What would it cost to ship this and when would it arrive?" (a quote for a parcel not yet sent) → SHIP_RATE_ETA_GENERAL. Not: "What appointment window did dispatch commit for this stop?" (the dispatch schedule) → DELIVERY_WINDOW_VERIFY_GENERAL.
intents.onchain_note: the intent has no response format

name: PAYMENT_METHOD_VERIFY
description: Verifies card BIN validity, tokenization credentials, bank account routing, and active account standing.

intents.name: PAYMENT_METHOD_VERIFY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies a card BIN, payment token, bank account or routing number and asks whether it is valid, active and issued by the stated institution. Example: "Is BIN 411111 a valid Visa, which issuer does it belong to, and is routing number 021000021 an active ACH route?" → PAYMENT_METHOD_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "Does this $2,400 purchase look like it will charge back?" (a risk score on a transaction) → TRANSACTION_RISK_GENERAL.

name: PRODUCT_AUTHENTICITY
description: Validates product provenance, serial numbers, and manufacturer anti-counterfeit records against authorized registries.

intents.name: PRODUCT_AUTHENTICITY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies a serial number, barcode, GTIN or product identifier and asks whether the item is genuine according to the manufacturer or an authorized registry. Example: "Is serial 8F2K-99213 a genuine unit in the brand registry, and does GTIN 00012345600012 resolve to this product?" → PRODUCT_AUTHENTICITY_GENERAL. Not: "Is this photo of the product AI-generated?" (media forensics) → MEDIA_FORENSIC_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "Is this certificate of authenticity document genuine?" (document integrity) → DOCUMENT_AUTHENTICITY_GENERAL.

name: PURCHASE_ORDER_VERIFY
description: Reconciles enterprise purchase orders with procurement approval workflows, vendor quotas, and budget allocations.

intents.name: PURCHASE_ORDER_VERIFY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a purchase order and asks whether it exists in the ERP with the stated vendor, amounts, approvals and budget allocation. Example: "Does PO-2231 exist for vendor Acme at $42,000, approved, and within the Q3 budget line?" → PURCHASE_ORDER_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "Do the invoice, the PO and the goods receipt all tie out?" (a multi-document reconciliation) → INVOICE_LEDGER_RECONCILE_GENERAL. Not: "Is Acme a legitimate supplier to onboard?" (vendor due diligence) → VENDOR_VERIFY_GENERAL.

name: REGRESSION_VERIFY
description: Runs automated test suite executions to confirm backward compatibility across modified service APIs and libraries.

intents.name: REGRESSION_VERIFY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks for an automated test suite to be run against a build, service or API and for the resulting pass/fail set, to confirm previously working behaviour still works. Example: "Run the end-to-end suite against build 4412 of the checkout API and report which tests fail versus the last green run." → REGRESSION_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "Does this patch build and fix the defect?" (verifying one specific patch) → CODE_PATCH_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "Did the service meet its uptime target last month?" (an SLA threshold) → SLA_COMPLIANCE_GENERAL.

name: REGULATORY_FILING_MONITOR
description: Parses statutory regulatory filings, 10-K/10-Q disclosures, and disclosure updates from financial oversight portals.

intents.name: REGULATORY_FILING_MONITOR_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names an issuer, ticker or regulator and asks whether a specific statutory filing has appeared, or for what it contains: 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, exchange disclosures. Example: "Has Tesla filed its latest 10-Q on SEC EDGAR, on what date was it accepted, and what did it disclose about margins?" → REGULATORY_FILING_MONITOR_GENERAL. Not: "What is Tesla's P/E ratio?" (market data, not the filing) → FINANCIAL_DATA_GENERAL. Not: "Is Tesla Inc registered and who are its directors?" (a company register record) → CORPORATE_REGISTRY_LOOKUP_GENERAL.

name: RETURN_POLICY_VERIFY
description: Validates order return eligibility, restocking fees, and merchant policy constraints based on purchase timestamp and category.

intents.name: RETURN_POLICY_VERIFY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies an order or purchase context and asks whether it can still be returned under the merchant's policy, and at what cost. Example: "This item shipped 40 days ago and was opened: is it still returnable under this merchant's policy, and what restocking fee applies?" → RETURN_POLICY_VERIFY_GENERAL. Not: "Verify order 114-3941-8820 exists with these line items and total." (order existence) → COMMERCE_PURCHASE_VERIFY_GENERAL.

name: ROUTE_ETA

intents.name: AGENT_TASK_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks about autonomous AI agent behavior specifically (tool use, taking actions, multi-step autonomy) as distinct from a standard chatbot, or is itself a request requiring autonomous multi-step action. Example: "How does an AI agent decide when to call a tool versus answering directly?" → AGENT_TASK_GENERAL. Not: "Book me a flight and then reserve a hotel." (a concrete multi-step task to execute, not a question about agent behavior) → TASK_COMPLETION_GENERAL.

intents.name: AI_TEXT_DETECTION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query provides a specific block of text and asks whether it was written by an AI or a human. The user must supply actual text content to analyze — a question that merely asks about AI detection conceptually (without providing text to analyze) is not this intent. Example: "Here's a paragraph: '...'. Was this written by an AI or a human?" → AI_TEXT_DETECTION_GENERAL. Not: "How do AI text detectors work?" (asks about the method conceptually, no text supplied to analyze) → CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL.

intents.name: CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL
intents.description: General knowledge, reasoning, explanation, or conversational question answerable directly without live data, external sources, or specialized tooling. This is the default/general-purpose intent when nothing more specific clearly fits — e.g. 'explain what X does.' Example: "Why is the sky blue?" → CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL. Not: "What's the current price of Bitcoin?" (needs live, external data) → CRYPTO_PRICE_USD or WEB_SEARCH_GENERAL.

intents.name: CONTENT_EXTRACTION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies unstructured content and asks for specific structured fields to be pulled out of it. Example: "Here's a receipt (as text): '...', extract the merchant name, date, and total amount." → CONTENT_EXTRACTION_GENERAL. Not: "What sentiment does this receipt's review comment express?" (asks for a judgment, not structured fields pulled out) → SENTIMENT_ANALYSIS_GENERAL.

intents.name: CONTENT_MODERATION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query is itself asking to classify, flag, or moderate a specific piece of provided content, OR asks how automated content moderation works as a method/technique — not merely a question that mentions moderation as an unrelated concept. Example: "Does this comment violate community guidelines: 'You're an idiot and should quit.'?" or "How do automated moderation systems detect hate speech?" → CONTENT_MODERATION_GENERAL. Not: "Should platforms moderate more content?" (an opinion/policy question that only mentions moderation as a topic) → CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL.

intents.name: CONTENT_VERIFICATION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks whether a specific piece of supplied content is genuine and unaltered, covering provenance and integrity generally rather than media forensics specifically. Example: "Here's the text of a press release: '...'. Is this the genuine, unaltered version the company issued, or has it been tampered with?" or "Here's a copy of a contract clause: '...'. Is this the original wording, or has it been altered?" → CONTENT_VERIFICATION_GENERAL. Not: "Is this image a deepfake?" (media-specific forensics question) → DEEPFAKE_DETECTION_GENERAL.

intents.name: CRYPTO_PRICE_USD
intents.description: Query names a cryptocurrency asset and asks for its CURRENT price in US dollars. Example: "What is the current price of Ethereum (ETH) in USD?" → CRYPTO_PRICE_USD. Not: "How much ETH does 0x6872...de hold?" (a balance, not a price) → WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK_GENERAL. Not: market cap or 24h volume (broader market data) → FINANCIAL_DATA_GENERAL.
intents.onchain_note: number field "price_usd" has no decimals

intents.name: CVE_LOOKUP_CVSS
intents.description: Query supplies a CVE identifier and asks for its CVSS severity score. Example: "What is the CVSS score of CVE-2021-44228?" → CVE_LOOKUP_CVSS. Not: "What are the most dangerous vulnerabilities this year?" (no CVE identifier) → WEB_SEARCH_GENERAL. Not: ranking a set of findings → VULNERABILITY_TRIAGE_GENERAL.

intents.name: DEEPFAKE_DETECTION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query includes an actual image or video URL/reference and specifically asks whether it is a deepfake or whether a face/person in it has been synthetically generated or swapped. Requires real attached media — the word 'deepfake' alone with no media reference does not qualify. Example: "Here's a video URL: [link]. Is the face in this a deepfake?" → DEEPFAKE_DETECTION_GENERAL. Not: "What is a deepfake and how are they made?" (conceptual question, no media referenced) → CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL.

intents.name: FACT_CHECK_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies a specific claim or statement and asks whether it is true, with supporting evidence. A general knowledge question is CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL — this intent requires a checkable claim. Example: "Is it true that drinking coffee stunts your growth? Verify this claim." → FACT_CHECK_GENERAL. Not: "Does coffee have any health effects?" (open-ended question, not a specific claim to verify) → CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL or WEB_SEARCH_GENERAL.

intents.name: FINANCIAL_DATA_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks for market data, company fundamentals, or financial statistics beyond a single quoted price. Example: "Give the market cap and 24h trading volume for token X on base." or "What is Apple's P/E ratio and revenue growth this quarter?" → FINANCIAL_DATA_GENERAL. Not: "What is the price of token X?" or "What is Apple's share price?" alone (single quoted price) → CRYPTO_PRICE_USD or STOCK_PRICE_US_EQUITY.

intents.name: FRAUD_DETECTION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks how likely a specific entity, transaction or action is to be fraudulent. Example: "How likely is it that this transaction from 0xabc123... is fraudulent?" or "Does this email asking me to wire money to a new account look like a scam?" → FRAUD_DETECTION_GENERAL. Not: "What is the status of transaction 0xabc123...?" (asks for transaction details, not a fraud likelihood judgment) → ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP_GENERAL.

intents.name: GAME_RESULT_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a specific completed sports fixture or competition and asks for its final outcome or winner. Distinct from an in-progress or live score, which is SPORTS_SCORE_GENERAL. Example: "Who won the Lakers vs Celtics game last night?" → GAME_RESULT_GENERAL. Not: "What's the current score in the Lakers vs Celtics game right now?" (still in progress) → SPORTS_SCORE_GENERAL.

intents.name: GAS_PRICE_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks for the current or recent transaction fee level on a named blockchain network. Distinct from the price of that chain's token, which is CRYPTO_PRICE_USD. Example: "What is the current gas price in Gwei on the Ethereum network?" or informally "Polygon fees felt high yesterday, what are they at now?" → GAS_PRICE_GENERAL. Not: a question with a similar 'it was X yesterday, what about now' shape but no blockchain network named → not GAS_PRICE_GENERAL (a network name like Polygon/Ethereum/Base is not a weather location, don't route this to WEATHER_FORECAST_GENERAL).

intents.name: IMAGE_VERIFICATION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query includes an actual image URL/reference and asks whether it has been digitally manipulated, edited, or spliced (distinct from asking if it's AI-generated outright — that's MEDIA_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK_GENERAL). Requires real attached media. Example: "Here's an image URL: [link]. Has this photo been edited or spliced?" → IMAGE_VERIFICATION_GENERAL. Not: "Here's an image URL: [link]. Is this AI-generated?" (asks if it's AI-generated outright, not edited/spliced) → MEDIA_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK_GENERAL.

intents.name: IP_GEOLOCATION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies an IP address and asks where it is located geographically. For abuse history, use THREAT_INTELLIGENCE_INDICATOR. Example: "Where is the IP address 8.8.8.8 located?" → IP_GEOLOCATION_GENERAL. Not: "Has the IP address 8.8.8.8 been flagged for abuse?" (asks about reputation/abuse history, not location) → IP_REPUTATION (if registered) or CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL.
intents.onchain_note: the intent has no response format

intents.name: LANGUAGE_GENERATION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks about how language generation works as a capability or technique, or requests free-form natural-language output from a described prompt. Prefer CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL for ordinary conversational questions. Example: "Explain how transformer-based language generation models decide the next word." → LANGUAGE_GENERATION_GENERAL. Not: "Write me a short poem about autumn." (an ordinary request for produced text) → TEXT_GENERATION_GENERAL.

intents.name: MEDIA_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK_GENERAL
intents.description: Query includes an actual image or video URL/reference and asks broadly whether it is authentic, real, or AI-generated. Words like 'authentic,' 'real,' 'validity,' or 'genuine' alone, with no actual media attached, do NOT qualify. Example: "Here's an image URL: [link]. Is this photo real or AI-generated?" → MEDIA_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK_GENERAL. Not: "What is the technical validity of X's claims?" (uses 'validity' but has no media reference at all) → WEB_SEARCH_GENERAL or CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL.

intents.name: NEWS_HEADLINES_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks for current news headlines for a topic or region, as a list rather than full articles. Example: "Give me today's top headlines about the tech industry." → NEWS_HEADLINES_GENERAL. Not: "Give me a detailed article about the latest tech industry merger." (wants full article content, not a headline list) → NEWS_SEARCH_GENERAL.

intents.name: NEWS_SEARCH_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks for news articles or coverage matching a topic, entity or time period. Prefer NEWS_HEADLINES_GENERAL when the user wants a headline list rather than article results. Example: "Find recent articles covering the merger between company X and company Y." → NEWS_SEARCH_GENERAL. Not: "Just give me the top headlines about company X." (wants a headline list, not article coverage) → NEWS_HEADLINES_GENERAL.

intents.name: ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies a transaction hash or names a specific on-chain transaction and asks for its details, status or effects. Requires an actual transaction reference, not a general question about how transactions work. Example: "What was the status and gas used of transaction 0xabc123...?" → ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP_GENERAL. Not: a question about a wallet's overall balance → WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK_GENERAL.

intents.name: RESEARCH_QUERY_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks a research question and expects an answer supported by citations to sources. Example: "What does the evidence say about the health effects of intermittent fasting? Cite your sources." → RESEARCH_QUERY_GENERAL. Not: "Summarize everything known about intermittent fasting across all major studies." (wants a broad multi-source synthesis, not a cited answer to one question) → RESEARCH_SYNTHESIS_GENERAL.

intents.name: RESEARCH_SYNTHESIS_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks to gather findings across multiple sources and synthesise them into a combined answer or summary, rather than returning a single fact or a list of links. Example: "Summarize what the latest studies say about coffee's effect on longevity, across multiple sources." → RESEARCH_SYNTHESIS_GENERAL. Not: "What's one study that looked at coffee and longevity?" (wants a single source/fact, not a synthesis) → RESEARCH_QUERY_GENERAL or WEB_SEARCH_GENERAL.

intents.name: SPORTS_SCORE_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a specific sports fixture, team or competition and asks for the current or most recent score. Distinct from asking who ultimately won a finished event, which is GAME_RESULT_GENERAL. Example: "What's the current score in the Lakers vs Celtics game right now?" → SPORTS_SCORE_GENERAL. Not: "Who won the Lakers vs Celtics game last night?" (event already concluded, asks for final outcome) → GAME_RESULT_GENERAL.
intents.onchain_note: the intent has no response format

intents.name: SSL_VERIFICATION_CERT
intents.description: Query supplies a hostname and asks whether its TLS/SSL certificate is currently valid and trusted. Example: "Is the SSL certificate for example.com valid?" → SSL_VERIFICATION_CERT. Not: "Is example.com a safe site to visit?" (general safety judgment) → URL_SCAN_VERDICT.

intents.name: STOCK_PRICE_US_EQUITY
intents.description: Query names a US-listed equity or its ticker and asks for the CURRENT share price in US dollars. A company mentioned in passing does not qualify. Example: "What is the current share price of Apple (AAPL)?" → STOCK_PRICE_US_EQUITY. Not: "Apple just released a new iPhone, will sales be strong?" (company named, no price asked) → CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL or WEB_SEARCH_GENERAL. Not: a historical price on a past date.
intents.onchain_note: number field "price_usd" has no decimals

intents.name: STORM_ALERT_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a specific, resolvable location and asks specifically about active or upcoming storm systems, high winds, or disruption risk from severe weather there — not general current conditions. Example: "Is there a hurricane warning in effect for Miami, Florida right now?" → STORM_ALERT_GENERAL. Not: a question with no resolvable location, even if it uses risk/disruption-sounding words like 'high,' 'surge,' or 'glitch' → do not route to STORM_ALERT_GENERAL just on word-shape; use CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL or WEB_SEARCH_GENERAL.

intents.name: TASK_COMPLETION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks about what makes an AI agent effective at completing multi-step tasks, or is itself a request to complete a defined multi-step task end-to-end. Example: "Book me a flight to New York and then reserve a hotel near the airport for those dates." → TASK_COMPLETION_GENERAL. Not: "How do AI agents decide which tool to call?" (asks about agent behavior/mechanics, not a request to perform a task) → AGENT_TASK_GENERAL.

intents.name: TELEGRAPH_KNOWLEDGE_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks about Telegraph, Telegraph protocol, its products, or ecosystem — including Alexandria (flagship intelligence layer), the Explorer (leaderboard, live feed, signal search), Hackathon, WASM/miner registration, intents, the Miner YAML Registry (integrate.telegraphprotocol.com), current miners or their details, and any applications built on Telegraph (TruthWire, TrustFilter, ScholarGuard, ReviewRadar). Also covers protocol fundamentals like tokenomics, architecture, documentation, earning, and how the system works. Also covers any question where the user addresses the assistant directly as "you" (e.g. "what can you do", "who are you", "how can I use you") — the assistant is Telegraph. Use this for ANY question related to Telegraph, its products, platforms, ecosystem, or the assistant itself, rather than routing to general CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL or WEB_SEARCH_GENERAL. Example: "What can you do?" or "How do I register a miner on Telegraph?" → TELEGRAPH_KNOWLEDGE_GENERAL. Not: "What can an AI agent do in general?" (asks about AI agents generically, not about Telegraph or the assistant itself) → AGENT_TASK_GENERAL or CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL.

intents.name: TEXT_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK_GENERAL
intents.description: Query supplies a block of text and asks whether it is genuine, original, or machine-generated. Where the user explicitly asks about AI authorship, prefer AI_TEXT_DETECTION_GENERAL. Example: "Here's an essay: '...'. Is this original writing or was it copied/plagiarized from somewhere else?" → TEXT_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK_GENERAL. Not: "Here's a paragraph: '...'. Was this written by an AI or a human?" (explicitly asks about AI authorship) → AI_TEXT_DETECTION_GENERAL.

intents.name: TEXT_GENERATION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks for free-form written output for a described task — drafting, rewriting, summarising or composing text. Prefer CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL when the user simply wants an answer rather than produced text. Example: "Write a short poem about autumn." or "Rewrite this paragraph to sound more formal." → TEXT_GENERATION_GENERAL. Not: "What makes a good poem?" (wants an answer/explanation, not produced text) → CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL.

intents.name: TOKEN_HOLDER_COUNT_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a specific token or contract address and asks how many distinct addresses hold it. Not a request for the token's price, supply or market data. Example: "How many distinct holder addresses does the ERC-20 token contract 0x8335...913 on base have?" → TOKEN_HOLDER_COUNT_GENERAL. Not: "How much ETH does 0x6872...de hold on ethereum?" (one address's own balance, not a headcount of holders) → WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK_GENERAL. Not: "How deep is this token's own trading liquidity in DEX pools? Give this token's pool liquidity in USD." (a liquidity/TVL question, not a holder count, even though it names a token contract) → TVL_LOOKUP_GENERAL.

intents.name: TVL_LOOKUP_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a specific DeFi protocol, pool or chain and asks for the total value locked in it. Distinct from a token's market capitalisation. Example: "For the token at contract 0x8335...913 on base, how deep is its own trading liquidity in DEX pools (e.g. Uniswap)? Give this token's pool liquidity in USD." → TVL_LOOKUP_GENERAL. Not: a question asking how many addresses hold a token → TOKEN_HOLDER_COUNT_GENERAL.

intents.name: TWITTER_SEARCH_GENERAL
intents.description: Query asks to search posts, accounts or discussion on X/Twitter specifically. A question that merely mentions Twitter as a topic does not qualify — the user must want results from the platform. Example: "What are people saying about the new iPhone launch on X/Twitter?" → TWITTER_SEARCH_GENERAL. Not: "Is Twitter/X profitable as a company?" (Twitter is the subject, not the source to search) → CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL or WEB_SEARCH_GENERAL.

intents.name: URL_SCAN_VERDICT
intents.description: Query supplies a URL and asks whether it is safe to visit, or whether it is a phishing or malware page. Example: "Is this URL safe to click: http://example.com/offer?" → URL_SCAN_VERDICT. Not: "Is example.com's SSL certificate valid?" (certificate details only) → SSL_VERIFICATION_CERT. Not: a file hash → MALWARE_DETECTION_HASH.

intents.name: VIDEO_VERIFICATION_GENERAL
intents.description: Query references an actual video file or URL and asks to verify its authenticity, origin, or whether it has been edited/deepfaked. The mere word 'video' in an unrelated question does not qualify — requires a real attached video. Example: "Here's a video URL: [link]. Can you verify its origin and whether it's been edited?" → VIDEO_VERIFICATION_GENERAL. Not: "What's the best video editing software?" (mentions 'video' but no actual video referenced to verify) → CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL or WEB_SEARCH_GENERAL.

intents.name: WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a specific blockchain address or ENS name and asks for its current native-coin or token balance on a named chain. A question that merely mentions a wallet without asking what it holds does not qualify. Example: "What is the balance of vitalik.eth on ethereum?" or "How much ETH does 0x6872...de hold on ethereum?" → WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK_GENERAL. ('How much does address X hold' is a balance question about that one address, even though it uses the word 'hold.') Not: "How many holders does USDC have on ethereum?" (asks about the token's holder population, not one address's own holdings) → TOKEN_HOLDER_COUNT_GENERAL.

intents.name: WEATHER_CHECK_TEMPERATURE
intents.description: Query names a specific, resolvable city and asks for the CURRENT air temperature there. Example: "What is the temperature in London right now?" → WEATHER_CHECK_TEMPERATURE. Not: a forecast for a future window (WEATHER_FORECAST_GENERAL). Not: a question with no resolvable location.

intents.name: WEATHER_FORECAST_GENERAL
intents.description: Query names a specific, resolvable location and asks for FUTURE weather conditions over a stated time window (e.g. 'next 24 hours'), not current conditions. Example: "What is the 24-hour weather forecast for Reykjavik, Iceland, including temperature, precipitation probability, and wind speed?" → WEATHER_FORECAST_GENERAL. Not: "Polygon fees felt high yesterday. What are they at now?" (no location, this is a blockchain network fee question, not weather) → GAS_PRICE_GENERAL. Not: "Will the US GPS glitch recur this year?" or "Will .name domain sales surge?" (no resolvable location, no weather content) → CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL or WEB_SEARCH_GENERAL. A 'yesterday vs now' or 'will X happen' sentence shape alone is NOT evidence of a weather question. The location and the atmospheric/fee/subject-matter content are what matter, not the tense.

intents.name: WEB_SEARCH_GENERAL
intents.description: Query needs current, live, or externally-sourced information not reliably answerable from static/training knowledge — general 'what is the current price of Bitcoin' questions that need up-to-date grounding. Example: "What's the latest news on the Fed's interest rate decision?" → WEB_SEARCH_GENERAL. Not: "Explain what an interest rate is." (answerable from general knowledge, no live data needed) → CHAT_COMPLETION_GENERAL.
